app.name: Runic SSH
connecting.auth.body: The prompt is open in a window of its own, because a secret must never enter the document that renders terminal output. Nothing has reached the host yet.
connecting.auth.title: Waiting on the credential
connecting.body: Opening the connection. The host key is checked before anything is sent, and the credential is asked for after that — never before.
connecting.title: Reaching {host}…
credential.failed: This prompt is no longer valid
credential.passphrase: Passphrase (leave empty if the key has none)
credential.remember: Remember this in the system keychain
credential.subject: {name} — {user}@{host}
credential.title: Authentication required
empty.hint: Pick a host on the left, or press {keys} for commands.
empty.pane.hint: Pick a tab above, or a host on the left.
empty.pane.title: No session in this pane
empty.title: No session open
failure.authentication.body: The password or key was not accepted for this user. Trying again asks for it afresh.
failure.authentication.title: The host refused the credential
failure.cancelled.body: The credential prompt was closed, so the connection was not made. Nothing was sent.
failure.cancelled.title: Cancelled
failure.certificate.body: This connection was refused. Runic SSH does not verify certificates yet.
failure.keyUnreadable.body: It is not a key in a format Runic SSH understands, or the passphrase does not open it.
failure.keyUnreadable.title: The private key could not be read
failure.keychain.body: The system keychain did not answer. You can still connect by typing the credential.
failure.keychain.title: The saved credential could not be read
failure.prompt.body: Nobody could have answered it, so the attempt was stopped rather than left waiting. This one is ours.
failure.prompt.title: The credential prompt could not open
failure.revoked.body: This connection was refused and cannot be accepted. Nothing was sent to the host.
failure.rsaRefused.body: A timing attack on RSA signing has no fixed version available, so Runic SSH will not sign with one. An Ed25519 or ECDSA key works. See ADR-0010.
failure.rsaRefused.title: RSA private keys are refused
failure.timeout.body: Something answered at that address, or nothing did, and the connection never finished. A firewall that drops the reply and a server too busy to complete the handshake both look like this.
failure.timeout.title: The host did not answer in time
failure.transport.body: The host answered, and the SSH conversation did not finish. It may have dropped the connection, or be running something that is not an SSH server.
failure.transport.title: The connection failed
failure.unexpected.body: Runic SSH does not have a better answer than this. The code below names the failure exactly, and belongs in a bug report.
failure.unexpected.title: The connection failed
failure.unknownSession.body: It was deleted, or the file it lives in was changed while the application was open.
failure.unknownSession.title: That session is gone
failure.unreachable.body: Nothing answered at that address and port. Check that the host is up, and that the port is the one it listens on.
failure.unreachable.title: Could not reach the host
group.close: Close every tab in this group
group.close.detail.one: One connected session will be disconnected
hostKey.certificate.body: known_hosts says {host} authenticates with a certificate. Runic SSH does not verify certificates yet, and trusting a bare key instead is exactly the substitution that marker warns about.
hostKey.certificate.title: This host uses a certificate
hostKey.changed.body: The key {host} presented does not match the one saved. Either the host was rebuilt, or something is sitting between you and it.
hostKey.changed.confirmPrompt: TO OVERRIDE, TYPE THE HOST NAME
hostKey.changed.title: Host key changed — connection blocked
hostKey.refused.note: Nothing was sent to the host
hostKey.revoked.body: known_hosts marks this key as revoked. It cannot be accepted, and there is no override.
hostKey.revoked.title: This key is revoked
hostKey.unknown.body: Runic SSH has never connected to {host} before. Confirm the fingerprint through a channel you already trust — not through this connection.
hostKey.unknown.title: Unknown host key
hostKey.verify.hint: From the provider console, a configuration repository, or someone who runs the host.
hostKey.verify.label: I verified this fingerprint out of band
palette.placeholder: Type a command or a host
palette.title: Command palette
rail.label: Activities
rail.settings.locked: Settings are held shut while you are typing into several hosts
session.editor.groupHint: Optional. Sessions are listed under it.
session.editor.name: Name
session.editor.nameHint: Leave empty to use the host
session.editor.noSecret: No password is stored here. You are asked for one when you connect, in a window of its own.
sessions.empty.body: Add a host to connect to. Nothing is sent anywhere until you do.
sessions.empty.title: No sessions yet
sessions.title: SESSIONS
settings.appearance.lead: How the application looks on this machine. Nothing here is sent anywhere.
settings.decorations.hint: Turn this on if the window cannot be moved or resized by your desktop.
settings.discard.title: This form has changes that were never saved.
settings.language.hint: Security warnings are reviewed by a native speaker; the English text is the one that decides when they disagree.
settings.sessions.lead: Saved hosts. No password is kept here; you are asked for one when you connect.
settings.sessions.pick: Pick a host to edit, or add one.
settings.title: Settings
tabs.editor.unsaved: Close the editor — it has unsaved changes
tabs.label: Open sessions
terminal.paste.body: The remote shell runs each line as it arrives, so this starts running before you press Return.
terminal.paste.body.one: Typing is synchronised, so this leaves the pane you are looking at and runs on every pane on screen.
terminal.paste.hosts: This is sent to {count} hosts at once.
terminal.paste.title: Paste {count} lines?
